items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Pressures on people and environments in cities, such as pollution, congestion, poor housing, crime and deprivation"?
items.answer: urban stress
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of urban stress.

items.stem: Explain why slum upgrading may be more effective than slum clearance.
items.answer: Upgrading keeps communities and livelihoods intact, gives secure tenure and improves services at lower cost; clearance destroys homes and social networks and often moves people to distant sites without jobs.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Upgrading keeps communities and livelihoods intact, gives secure tenure and improves services at lower cost; clearance destroys homes and social networks and often moves people to distant sites without jobs. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims: "All residents of informal settlements are unemployed." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Most residents work, often in the informal sector, and many settlements are economically productive (e.g. Dharavi).
items.markingKey: Most residents work, often in the informal sector, and many settlements are economically productive (e.g. Dharavi). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Suggest two indicators that could be used to map deprivation in a city.
items.answer: Unemployment rate, income, educational attainment, life expectancy or illness rates, crime rates, overcrowding.
items.markingKey: Unemployment rate, income, educational attainment, life expectancy or illness rates, crime rates, overcrowding.

items.stem: A fieldwork survey recorded land-use categories recorded at 60 random sample points in central Hanoi: residential 6, commercial 40, industrial 3, open space 11. Test the null hypothesis that there is no preference between categories using the chi-squared test (χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E; critical value at 0.05 for 3 degrees of freedom = 7.81).
items.answer: E = 15 per category; χ² = 57.73; df = 3; significant - reject the null hypothesis
items.markingKey: M1 expected 60/4 = 15; M1 Σ(O − E)²/E; A1 χ² = 57.73; A1 df = 3; R1 compare with 7.81: reject H₀.

items.stem: The following household water use (litres per person per day) from a questionnaire in Lima were recorded: 51, 94, 259, 208, 115, 154, 125, 157, 232, 207, 132. Calculate the median, the interquartile range (quartiles as medians of the lower and upper halves) and the standard deviation (σ = √(Σ(x − x̄)²/n)).
items.markingKey: A1 median 154; M1 quartiles from ordered data (Q1 115, Q3 208); A1 IQR 93; M1 A1 σ = 60.12.

items.stem: Give one strength and one weakness of the claim that urban stresses are mainly caused by rapid population growth.
items.answer: Growth adds pressure, but governance and inequality largely determine whether stress results.
items.markingKey: For: growth exceeds housing and infrastructure (Lagos, Dhaka). Against: governance, planning and inequality determine outcomes (Singapore is dense but well managed). [4]: 1 mark for a valid argument for, 1 for its development; 1 mark for a valid argument against, 1 for its development; generic points without geographical context are capped at 2.

items.stem: Define the term "urban social segregation".
items.answer: The separation of different social, ethnic or income groups into distinct residential areas
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the separation of different social, ethnic or income groups into distinct residential areas. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain why deprivation tends to be concentrated in particular parts of a city.
items.answer: Low incomes restrict housing choices to cheap areas; cumulative disadvantage - poor schools, health, crime and unemployment - reinforces itself; discrimination and housing policy concentrate groups.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Low incomes restrict housing choices to cheap areas; cumulative disadvantage - poor schools, health, crime and unemployment - reinforces itself; discrimination and housing policy concentrate groups. items.stem: Distinguish between urban environmental stress and urban social stress.
items.answer: Environmental stresses include air and water pollution, waste and noise; social stresses include crime, deprivation, overcrowding and segregation.
items.markingKey: Environmental stresses include air and water pollution, waste and noise; social stresses include crime, deprivation, overcrowding and segregation. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With reference to Lagos traffic, explain how it illustrates traffic congestion.
items.answer: Residents can spend several hours a day commuting, and the Lagos Blue Line light rail opened in 2023. Rapid growth without mass transit created chronic congestion.
items.markingKey: Context (Residents can spend several hours a day commuting, and the Lagos Blue Line light rail opened in 2023.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.answer: A layer of warm air above cooler surface air that traps pollutants near the ground

items.stem: Ingrid writes: "The urban heat island is strongest during hot summer afternoons." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The urban-rural difference is usually greatest on calm, clear nights when rural areas cool rapidly.
items.markingKey: The urban-rural difference is usually greatest on calm, clear nights when rural areas cool rapidly. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why cities may receive more rainfall than surrounding areas.
items.answer: Heat islands create convection; pollutant particles provide condensation nuclei; tall buildings increase turbulence - so thunderstorms are more frequent downwind.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Heat islands create convection; pollutant particles provide condensation nuclei; tall buildings increase turbulence - so thunderstorms are more frequent downwind. items.stem: Suggest two reasons why the heat island is a growing health risk.
items.answer: Climate change increases heatwave frequency and intensity; ageing urban populations are more vulnerable; night-time heat prevents recovery, increasing mortality.
items.markingKey: Climate change increases heatwave frequency and intensity; ageing urban populations are more vulnerable; night-time heat prevents recovery, increasing mortality.

items.stem: Incoming shortwave radiation is 300 W/m². A surface of cropland (albedo 0.2) is replaced by grassland (albedo 0.25). Calculate the change in absorbed radiation and explain its significance for climate feedbacks.
items.answer: Absorbed changes from 240.0 to 225.0 W/m², a change of -15.0 W/m²; less energy absorbed - a cooling effect.
items.markingKey: M1 (1 − albedo) × incoming for both; A1 240.0 and 225.0; A1 change -15.0 W/m²; R1 feedback explained.

items.stem:
Study the infographic / visual stimulus described below.

Transect data, Paris at 23:00 on a calm summer night - city centre 26.8 °C; 3 km 26.1 °C; 6 km 25.0 °C; 10 km 23.4 °C; 15 km (rural) 20.9 °C.

(b) Using the resource and your own knowledge, suggest two reasons why the difference is greatest at night. [6]
items.answer: (a) Intensity = 26.8 − 20.9 = 5.9 °C; gradient = 5.9/15 = 0.39 °C per km (b) Urban materials release heat stored during the day; rural areas cool quickly by radiation under clear skies; calm conditions prevent mixing.

items.stem: Distinguish between a low emission zone and a congestion charge.
items.answer: A congestion charge charges all vehicles entering a zone to cut traffic volume; a low emission zone charges or bans only the most polluting vehicles to improve air quality.

items.answer: Vegetation shades surfaces and cools air through evapotranspiration, has higher albedo than asphalt and stores less heat; Medellín's green corridors reduced local temperatures by about 2 °C.

items.stem: Explain how smart technology can make cities more sustainable.
items.answer: Sensors and data optimise traffic signals, public transport, street lighting, energy grids and leak detection, reducing congestion, energy use and waste; apps encourage sharing and active travel.

Pressures on people and environments in cities, such as pollution, congestion, poor housing, crime and deprivation

items.stem: Distinguish between top-down urban planning and bottom-up urban planning.
items.answer: Top-down planning is directed by governments or developers (Masdar, Songdo); bottom-up planning involves residents and communities (participatory budgeting in Porto Alegre).
items.markingKey: Top-down planning is directed by governments or developers (Masdar, Songdo); bottom-up planning involves residents and communities (participatory budgeting in Porto Alegre). items.stem: Distinguish between an eco-city and a smart city.
items.answer: A smart city focuses on digital technology and data to improve services; an eco-city focuses on environmental sustainability through design, energy and green space - a city can be one without the other.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "urban heat island (UHI)"?
options: The capacity of a city's people, institutions and systems to survive, adapt and grow despite chronic stresses and acute shocks

The phenomenon whereby urban areas are warmer than surrounding rural areas, especially at night
A city that uses digital technology, sensors and data to manage services such as transport, energy and water more efficiently

items.stem: To what extent is it true that traffic management strategies are the most effective way to improve urban air quality? Refer to places and scales you have studied.
items.answer: Traffic measures are essential but must be part of a broader strategy covering all sources.
items.markingKey: Indicative content - arguments supporting the statement: vehicles are a major NO₂ and PM source; London's ULEZ and Singapore ERP worked; can be targeted and quick. Arguments challenging it: heating, industry and regional sources must also be tackled (Beijing coal, Delhi crop burning); public transport and land-use planning are needed. Evaluation should weigh places, scales, perspectives and time. Judgement: Traffic measures are essential but must be part of a broader strategy covering all sources. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "urban stress"?
options: Pressures on people and environments in cities, such as pollution, congestion, poor housing, crime and deprivation
The capacity of a city's people, institutions and systems to survive, adapt and grow despite chronic stresses and acute shocks
The separation of different social, ethnic or income groups into distinct residential areas
A layer of warm air above cooler surface air that traps pollutants near the ground
items.answer: Pressures on people and environments in cities, such as pollution, congestion, poor housing, crime and deprivation
items.markingKey: A. "urban stress" is pressures on people and environments in cities, such as pollution, congestion, poor housing, crime and deprivation.

items.stem: London's Ultra Low Emission Zone (ULEZ) was introduced in central London in:
items.markingKey: D. It was expanded to all London boroughs in August 2023.

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "smart city".
items.answer: A city that uses digital technology, sensors and data to manage services such as transport, energy and water more efficiently
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a city that uses digital technology, sensors and data to manage services such as transport, energy and water more efficiently. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Omar writes: "Slums are only found in low-income countries." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Informal and substandard housing also exists in high-income countries, e.g. homeless encampments and informal settlements in Europe and the USA.
items.markingKey: Informal and substandard housing also exists in high-income countries, e.g. homeless encampments and informal settlements in Europe and the USA. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims: "The urban heat island is strongest during hot summer afternoons." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: The urban-rural difference is usually greatest on calm, clear nights when rural areas cool rapidly.
items.markingKey: The urban-rural difference is usually greatest on calm, clear nights when rural areas cool rapidly. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why some eco-city projects have struggled.
items.answer: High costs, top-down design that ignores residents, economic downturns (Masdar after 2008), difficulty attracting people and businesses, and a focus on technology rather than social needs.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: High costs, top-down design that ignores residents, economic downturns (Masdar after 2008), difficulty attracting people and businesses, and a focus on technology rather than social needs. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between slum upgrading and slum clearance.
items.answer: Clearance demolishes informal settlements and relocates residents; upgrading improves services, housing and tenure in place, often with resident participation.
items.markingKey: Clearance demolishes informal settlements and relocates residents; upgrading improves services, housing and tenure in place, often with resident participation. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the causes of the urban heat island effect.
items.answer: Dark surfaces (low albedo) absorb more radiation; concrete and asphalt store heat and release it at night; less vegetation and water mean less evapotranspiration; heat from vehicles, buildings and air-conditioning; urban canyons trap longwave radiation; pollution increases absorption.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Dark surfaces (low albedo) absorb more radiation; concrete and asphalt store heat and release it at night; less vegetation and water mean less evapotranspiration; heat from vehicles, buildings and air-conditioning; urban canyons trap longwave radiation; pollution increases absorption. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "Smart cities are automatically sustainable." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Technology can improve efficiency, but sustainability also needs social equity, affordable housing and low-carbon lifestyles; smart systems can raise privacy and inclusion concerns.
items.markingKey: Technology can improve efficiency, but sustainability also needs social equity, affordable housing and low-carbon lifestyles; smart systems can raise privacy and inclusion concerns. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A fieldwork survey recorded reasons for moving given by 80 migrants interviewed in Dubai: employment 30, family 21, education 9, housing 20. Test the null hypothesis that there is no preference between categories using the chi-squared test (χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E; critical value at 0.05 for 3 degrees of freedom = 7.81).
items.answer: E = 20 per category; χ² = 11.10; df = 3; significant - reject the null hypothesis
items.markingKey: M1 expected 80/4 = 20; M1 Σ(O − E)²/E; A1 χ² = 11.10; A1 df = 3; R1 compare with 7.81: reject H₀.
